## Bug Analysis & Fix Summary

### Root Cause

In **`CustomAuthenticatedSlide.java`**, the `isPolicyRespected()` method controls when the "Done" button is enabled during first-time setup. The `AppIntro2` framework uses this policy method to gate slide navigation.

The buggy code at lines 108-113:
```java
case CustomAuthenticationSlide.CRYPT_TYPE_PASS:
    if (EditTextHelper.getEditTextChars(_textPassword).length > 0) {
        return EditTextHelper.areEditTextsEqual(_textPassword, _textPasswordConfirm) || _checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked();
    }
    return false;
```

**The `|| _checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked()` condition** was the defect. When the user checks "show password":
1. The `setOnCheckedChangeListener` disables `_textPasswordConfirm`, leaving it empty
2. `areEditTextsEqual()` would return `false` (empty confirmation vs filled password)
3. The `|| _checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked()` short-circuits and returns `true` regardless

This allowed users to bypass the password confirmation entirely by simply checking "show password."

### Fix Applied

Changed the password case to **always require password confirmation**, regardless of visibility state:

```java
case CustomAuthenticationSlide.CRYPT_TYPE_PASS:
    return EditTextHelper.getEditTextChars(_textPassword).length > 0
            && EditTextHelper.areEditTextsEqual(_textPassword, _textPasswordConfirm);
```

Now the user must always enter the same password in both fields. The "show password" checkbox only controls text visibility — it no longer affects the validation logic.

### Build Note

The project build cannot complete in this environment because the Android Gradle Plugin 3.5.3 is not cached and the build environment has no network access. However, the Java fix is syntactically correct and logically sound.

**Patch** (relative to project root):

```diff
--- a/app/src/main/java/com/beemdevelopment/aegis/ui/slides/CustomAuthenticatedSlide.java
+++ b/app/src/main/java/com/beemdevelopment/aegis/ui/slides/CustomAuthenticatedSlide.java
@@ -105,11 +105,8 @@ public class CustomAuthenticatedSlide extends Fragment implements ISlidePolicy,
                 }
                 // intentional fallthrough
             case CustomAuthenticationSlide.CRYPT_TYPE_PASS:
-                if (EditTextHelper.getEditTextChars(_textPassword).length > 0) {
-                    return EditTextHelper.areEditTextsEqual(_textPassword, _textPasswordConfirm) || _checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked();
-                }
-
-                return false;
+                return EditTextHelper.getEditTextChars(_textPassword).length > 0
+                        && EditTextHelper.areEditTextsEqual(_textPassword, _textPasswordConfirm);
             default:
                 return false;
         }
```

            && EditTextHelper.areEditTextsEqual(_textPassword, _textPasswordConfirm);
```

Now the user must always enter the same password in both fields. The "show password" checkbox only controls text visibility — it no longer affects the validation logic.
